blocks.text: Nitric oxide and nitrogen dioxide are represented by NOx. They are generally produced from burning fossil fuels: at high temperature N2 + O2 gives 2NO (nitric oxide), and 2NO + O2 gives 2NO2 (nitrogen dioxide). Natural sources of N2O include microbial processes in soil and oceans where bacteria break down nitrogen compounds; human sources include agriculture (synthetic fertilisers) and industrial processes (combustion of fossil fuels). N2O depletes the ozone layer, and increased N2O contributes to climate change and affects air quality.

blocks.prompt: Why does burning fuel produce nitrogen oxides although fuels contain little nitrogen?
blocks.explanation: The high temperature of combustion makes the nitrogen and oxygen of the air itself combine, N2 + O2 giving 2NO, and the nitric oxide is then oxidised in the exhaust and the air to nitrogen dioxide.

items: NOx = NO + NO2 from fuel combustion (N2 + O2 gives 2NO at high temperature; 2NO + O2 gives 2NO2); N2O from microbes, fertilisers and combustion depletes ozone and warms the climate.
